top_choice_rationale: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a molecular design achievement (pKa-tuned charge switching plus controlled lipid self-assembly) that solves packaging and cytosolic release of large nucleic acids, with approved medicines at global scale and transfer to gene-editing delivery and other nanomedicine. A citation confined to the delivery chemistry avoids duplicating the 2023 Medicine prize; Cullis, Hope and Anderson cover the Vancouver design work and the combinatorial lipid lineage, though Madden, MacLachlan and Langer are left out.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly is general, and no direct tie to the lipid nanoparticle laureates is apparent
